title: AP Precalculus — Simultaneous Equations Recap
question: 12 systems of two linear equations, solve for x and y: Easy (add, substitute), Medium (scale one equation), Hard (scale both, negative and fraction answers).
intro:
**12 systems: 4 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.** Each has two equations and one pair \((x,\ y)\) that fits both.

- **Substitution:** when one equation gives \(y\) (or \(x\)) on its own, put it into the other.
- **Elimination:** scale one or both equations so one variable has opposite coefficients, then add.
- Always put the pair back into **both** equations before choosing A–D.

**Work on paper, then pick the pair.**

questions.title: Add the equations
questions.prompt:
Solve for \(x\) and \(y\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
x + y &= 7 \\
x - y &= 1
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Add the two equations: the \(y\) terms cancel.

\[
\begin{aligned}
(x + y) + (x - y) &= 7 + 1 \\
2x &= 8 \\
x &= 4
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(x = 4\) into the first equation.

\[
\begin{aligned}
4 + y &= 7 \\
y &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Check in the second: \(4 - 3 = 1\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(4,\ 3)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: y is already given
questions.prompt:
Solve for \(x\) and \(y\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
y &= 2x \\
x + y &= 9
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Replace \(y\) by \(2x\) in the second equation.

\[
\begin{aligned}
x + 2x &= 9 \\
3x &= 9 \\
x &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(y = 2x = 6\).

Check: \(3 + 6 = 9\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(3,\ 6)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Substitute y
questions.prompt:
Solve for \(x\) and \(y\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
x + y &= 10 \\
y &= x + 4
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Replace \(y\) by \(x + 4\) in the first equation.

\[
\begin{aligned}
x + (x + 4) &= 10 \\
2x + 4 &= 10 \\
2x &= 6 \\
x &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(y = 3 + 4 = 7\).

Check: \(3 + 7 = 10\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(3,\ 7)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Add to cancel x
questions.prompt:
Solve for \(x\) and \(y\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
2x + y &= 11 \\
y - x &= 2
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
From the second equation, \(y = x + 2\). Put it into the first.

\[
\begin{aligned}
2x + (x + 2) &= 11 \\
3x + 2 &= 11 \\
3x &= 9 \\
x &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(y = 3 + 2 = 5\).

Check: \(2(3) + 5 = 11\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(3,\ 5)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Scale one equation
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Multiply the second equation by \(3\) so the \(y\) terms match.

\[
\begin{aligned}
3x - 3y &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Add it to the first equation.

\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x + 3y) + (3x - 3y) &= 12 + 3 \\
5x &= 15 \\
x &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Then from \(x - y = 1\): \(y = 2\).

Check: \(2(3) + 3(2) = 12\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(3,\ 2)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Scale and subtract
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Multiply the second equation by \(2\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
2x + 2y &= 12
\end{aligned}
\]

Subtract it from the first.

\[
\begin{aligned}
(3x + 2y) - (2x + 2y) &= 16 - 12 \\
x &= 4
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(y = 6 - 4 = 2\).

Check: \(3(4) + 2(2) = 16\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(4,\ 2)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Opposite y coefficients
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
The \(y\) terms are already opposites. Add.

\[
\begin{aligned}
(5x - 2y) + (x + 2y) &= 4 + 8 \\
6x &= 12 \\
x &= 2
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(x = 2\) into the second.

\[
\begin{aligned}
2 + 2y &= 8 \\
2y &= 6 \\
y &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Check: \(5(2) - 2(3) = 4\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(2,\ 3)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Substitute from the simpler one
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
From the second equation, \(y = 2x - 2\). Put it into the first.

\[
\begin{aligned}
3x + 4(2x - 2) &= 25 \\
3x + 8x - 8 &= 25 \\
11x &= 33 \\
x &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(y = 2(3) - 2 = 4\).

Check: \(3(3) + 4(4) = 25\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(3,\ 4)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Negative solution
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Multiply the first equation by \(2\) so the \(y\) terms are opposites.

\[
\begin{aligned}
6x + 4y &= -2
\end{aligned}
\]

Add to the second.

\[
\begin{aligned}
(6x + 4y) + (5x - 4y) &= -2 + 13 \\
11x &= 11 \\
x &= 1
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(x = 1\) into the first.

\[
\begin{aligned}
3 + 2y &= -1 \\
2y &= -4 \\
y &= -2
\end{aligned}
\]

Check: \(5(1) - 4(-2) = 5 + 8 = 13\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(1,\ -2)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Scale both equations
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Make the \(y\) coefficients \(10\) and \(-10\): first \(\times2\), second \(\times5\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
4x + 10y &= -8 \\
15x - 10y &= 65
\end{aligned}
\]

Add.

\[
\begin{aligned}
19x &= 57 \\
x &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(x = 3\) into the first original equation.

\[
\begin{aligned}
6 + 5y &= -4 \\
5y &= -10 \\
y &= -2
\end{aligned}
\]

Check: \(3(3) - 2(-2) = 9 + 4 = 13\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(3,\ -2)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: Fractions first
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Clear the fractions: multiply the first equation by \(6\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
3x + 2y &= 24
\end{aligned}
\]

From the second, \(y = x - 3\). Substitute.

\[
\begin{aligned}
3x + 2(x - 3) &= 24 \\
5x - 6 &= 24 \\
5x &= 30 \\
x &= 6
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(y = 6 - 3 = 3\).

Check: \(\tfrac{6}{2} + \tfrac{3}{3} = 3 + 1 = 4\). ✓

\[
\boxed{(6,\ 3)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

questions.title: A fraction answer
questions.solution_title: Elimination or substitution, then check both equations
questions.solution:
Multiply the second equation by \(2\) so the \(y\) terms are opposites.

\[
\begin{aligned}
10x - 4y &= 50
\end{aligned}
\]

Add to the first.

\[
\begin{aligned}
(3x + 4y) + (10x - 4y) &= 2 + 50 \\
13x &= 52 \\
x &= 4
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(x = 4\) into the first.

\[
\begin{aligned}
12 + 4y &= 2 \\
4y &= -10 \\
y &= -\tfrac{5}{2}
\end{aligned}
\]

Check: \(5(4) - 2\left(-\tfrac{5}{2}\right) = 20 + 5 = 25\). ✓

\[
\boxed{\left(4,\ -\tfrac{5}{2}\right)}
\]

- The swapped pair and the sign-flipped pair fail one of the equations: always check both.

takeaway: Make one variable disappear, solve the one left, then go back for the other. Check both equations.
